chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan — meaning Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) — 'Is it permissible to eat the meat of the elephant?' So he said: 'No.' I said: 'And why?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because it is a transformed creature (mathula), and God — Mighty and Majestic — has forbidden the morphed ones (amsakh) and the flesh of what has been transformed in their forms.'

key_terms.الْأَمْسَاخُ: The morphed/transformed ones; plural of maskh — beings (humans or jinn) that were transformed into animal form as divine punishment
key_terms.مَثُلَةٌ: A creature that has been transformed (maskhah); a being that serves as a cautionary likeness or punishment-form
key_terms.مُثِّلَ بِهِ: What was transformed/made to resemble; refers to animals that are believed to be the transformed versions of sinners

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia Islam to eat elephant meat?
ai.summary: Al-Husayn ibn Khalid directly asked Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) — the seventh Imam — whether eating elephant meat is permissible. The Imam replied in the negative, explaining that the elephant is a 'mathula' (a creature that was transformed as divine punishment) and God has prohibited both the 'amsakh' (beings transformed from human form as a divine penalty) and the flesh of what was similarly transformed. This ruling is rooted in a cosmological theology in which certain animals, like the pig, bear, monkey, and elephant, are understood to be human souls transformed by God's wrath.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is it Permissible to eat the meat of the elephant?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. I said, ‘And why?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because it is a resemblance, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Prohibited the morphed ones, and the meat of what has been transformed by it in its image’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Amr ibn ‘ Uthman from al-Husayn ibn Khalid who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, Musa ibn Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the flesh of elephants. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not lawful for food.’ I then asked, ‘Why is it so?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It has deformities and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has made what is metamorphosed unlawful for food as well as the flesh of what is deformed in its shape.”’
